speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We are living in a world where industries and businesses are swarmed by digital disruption.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Yet, the infocomm industry and technology-based startups that have emerged could form a key growth sector of our future economy, as it provides good jobs, stronger businesses and a better quality of life in general.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: These projections provide us with an idea of the magnitude of digital disruption in the future.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Given our small and open economy, our businesses need to be nimble and embrace the transformation required to adapt to the new digital world.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What is the Government doing to ensure that Singapore's businesses and workforce are able to thrive in the digital future?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The Ministry has launched several initiatives to help the various industries transform and thrive in the digital era.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Can the Ministry update us on how these initiatives have performed?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Perhaps we can also learn on what more can be done to help our SMEs go digital?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Besides logistics and retail, what other sectors will be considered for digital transformation?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, for the ICM sector specifically, how do we help it grow and realise its full potential?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What are the Ministry’s areas of focus in helping Singapore companies to develop the ICM subsectors?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For these companies to be successful, we must help them internationalise.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We must help our local companies go international and leverage one another.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How is the Infocomm Media Development Authority's (IMDA’s) internationalisation effort progressing?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How is IMDA's approach for the internationalisation of ICM companies differentiated for the ICM sector, compared to that of International Enterprise (IE) Singapore for companies across other sectors?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Chairman, we recently passed the Cybersecurity Bill in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But our defences will only be as good as the ecosystem that we can build here, that is the CII providers, technology solution providers, manpower, startups and research and development (R&D).

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Singapore, as an international hub and global business and tourist destination, has been successful because of our connectivity.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How can the Government ensure that Singapore continues to maintain its lead in digital connectivity, given the environment around where all our competitors are also linking up?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Since ICM separates itself − it is a vibrant and growing sector for us and also one that has impact on other industries and our overall business and SME landscape – we should help aim to grow it to the best of our resources and provide opportunities at various levels for Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Mr Chairman, please allow me to continue my speech in Malay.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In Malay):   Digital skills have become a fundamental and important asset in today’s economy and for the future.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Many careers and businesses depend not only on digital technology but also relevant skills, like data analysis, in order to compete.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Without digital knowledge and skills, career progression will be hampered and the way businesses are done will also be limited.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We have no other choice and must undergo this transformation to survive in the future.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In the business world, we saw a trend of more Malay entrepreneurs moving to online platforms to conduct their business as well as grow their companies, not only for the local market but also regionally and globally.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, much more can be done for them to progress and be identified as a regional and global player.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The same goes for businessmen in areas, such as food and beverage (F&B), retail and logistics, who need to utilise digital technology and data analysis skills.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Such digital skills, at least at the basic level, must be acquired by workers at all levels, including professionals.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is also important for those who are entering the workforce, regardless of industry.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Every job, be it technicians or professionals, needs digital skills in order to perform their roles more effectively and productively in this digital era.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In terms of info-comm careers, many opportunities have been made available currently to help prepare for a digital future.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In fact, MCI estimated that this sector requires thousands of info-comm workers in a few years’ time.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Apart from workers, businessmen will also need to look at this trend and how it can affect their businesses, if they fail to make immediate preparations for this digital world.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Some of them have to engage in partnerships, for instance, when entering the global market, in order to become more effective.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
text: With the improvements in machine learning, AI can enhance its accuracy in diagnostic work, facilitate intelligent surveillance round the clock, and improve productivity through the reduction of manpower and the streamlining of work processes.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Mr Chairman, my cut today is on the digital economy as well.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Over the last two decades, digital computing technologies have rapidly changed the world, with far-ranging implications on businesses and consumers.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Particularly, the pace of adoption of digital technologies has accelerated over the recent years.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Adoption of digital technologies has resulted in a very connected world, empowering individuals and transforming how businesses and governments operate.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: There are many benefits to a digital economy.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Higher productivity, enhanced quality of life, better jobs, and the list goes on.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: There are many reasons to be optimistic about Singapore’s future in such an economy if we get a few core strategies right.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: This is a subject which I will return to discuss later.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Traditional factors of production like land, labour and capital will no longer constrain the economic expansion of a small island state like Singapore.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Goods can be produced and can be sold anywhere through e-commerce.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Through the Internet, we can also access labour anywhere.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: American high school teachers are teaching English Language to primary school students in China through the Internet.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: This has become a thriving business for companies like VIPKID, which provides international elementary school experience to half a million registered Chinese students online.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Capital can be raised in any stock exchanges through angel investors, venture capitalists or even through crowdfunding.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: All one needs is a sound business idea and persuasive skills.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: So, instead of land, labour and capital as traditional factors of production, we are now seeing a new factor of production.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: They are compartmentalised and do not lend themselves to analyses or deep insights which can help reduce pain points, improve asset utilisation or provide for a more tailored and customised service.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Chairman, knowledge convergence has been a key trend in the media for a number of years.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The blurring of the line between content creation and content distribution has profoundly changed the challenge that regulators face.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In the "good old days", film and television (TV) students made content; broadcasters and cinemas distributed them; and the average man on the street consumed the content.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Nowadays, everybody is both a consumer and the producer of content, using platforms like Facebook, Instagram or YouTube to share the content they create with the entire world.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It is in some ways amazing that these open platforms give each individual so much power to communicate with the world.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Anybody, even a young child, can go viral if they create good content.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: However, this openness creates its own challenges, since the platforms do not own the content that they carry.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: If objectionable content is found on YouTube or Facebook, it is not always easy to assign responsibility and have it removed.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We have continued advances in AI, and additional complication arises in the form of bots.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: They are programs which masquerade as real humans, adding to the noise on the Internet.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: These can have serious consequences, as the recent revelations about the impact of Russian bots on the US elections show.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Chairman, we recently debated the Cybersecurity Bill in Parliament which looks at 11 CII systems.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Our regular businesses and individuals also need to practise cybersecurity.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Given how plugged in we are as a country and as a people, every computer in our system can become a conduit in which to launch cyberattacks.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: They store them on computers, write them down or use the same password for multiple accounts.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The risks to us as a country is thus large as there are many open gateways through which we can be hacked.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How then can the Government work with businesses and educate the public on how to prevent and respond to cybersecurity threats and incidents?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: As we work with SMEs to encourage them to leverage digitalisation to increase productivity, can we also take the opportunity to educate them on cybersecurity and encourage them to take appropriate precautions?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Can the SME Centres set up to help SMEs embrace digitalisation also be equipped to provide cybersecurity awareness training to SMEs?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: For the public, can we work on two groups of individuals in particular?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: To the elderly who may give out personal details freely when asked, can we work through grassroots organisations to provide fundamental cybersecurity awareness to them?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And to our young who will use online resources increasingly in schools, can we include cybersecurity training as part of their school curriculum?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: CSA launched the "Live Savvy with Cybersecurity" campaign last year.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Such general awareness campaigns are useful to inculcate awareness of cyber threats to mass audiences.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Then we can discuss the steps we can take collectively to avoid being victims of cyberattacks.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Given the close to 180,000 SMEs we have in Singapore, how can we promote wider adoption of digital technologies?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: If we can encourage the adoption of digital technologies effectively by our SMEs, the training our workers can receive in the process will be a huge plus.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The Government has worked with the trade associations and chambers (TACs) to establish Digital Tech Hubs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Based on our knowledge of the most frequent queries SMEs have when they approach the Digital Tech Hubs, are we able to put together learning points, customise solutions and push out to a larger group of SMEs?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The Logistics IDP and the Retail IDP have been rolled out.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: What is helpful with the IDPs is that they include a self-assessment category which allows SMEs to know where the skill gaps are and then it directs the SMEs to look for help from Business Advisors at SME Centres or, in the case of needing advanced digital advisory, that they meet with principal consultants at SME Digital Tech Hub.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: On paper, the IDPs would give management consultants a run for their money and truly showcase the professionalism and high standards of the Civil Service.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: However, I am concerned with the rollout on the ground as many SME business owners may not read or understand the IDPs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How would the Government go about pushing out the IDPs on a broad scale?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Are there plans to go to the ground level to push the message out rather than wait for the SMEs to show up at the SME Centres or Digital Tech Hubs?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Would the Ministry be looking to roll out with certain Queen Bee companies in each sector to seed the digital plan and have it permeate through the supply chain?

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Mr Chairman, for many SMEs, going digital is a very difficult decision to make but it is a very critical one.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: For some, they look at it as a disruption but, for others who are successful, it is an opportunity.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: The SMEs Go Digital Programme that is under MCI has certainly made some headway but there are more that we can do.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: SMEs can implement information technology (IT) in two different ways: (a) internal, which is a process change in order to become leaner and save on manpower and become more cost-efficient; (b) external, which is to really change their business model, so that their products and services can be sold or marketed more efficiently.

speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It is an important part for them to shift their mindset, not just on process change.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: If there was one buzz word that has been hogging the news, it is the efforts of our Government to go digital.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We went from transport to financial sector, then down to the grassroots from buying groceries to buying food at the hawker centres and wet markets, and we have also been pushing very hard to get everyone on board.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The aim is to enhance productivity through tools, such as digital ordering and payment and fleet management, as well as cybersecurity, data protection and data analytics.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The Government has also offered consultants at the SME Digital Tech Hub who will go beyond providing basic advice on proven digital solutions that are pre-approved for funding support.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The TechSkills Accelerator (TeSA) is a SkillsFuture initiative driven by IMDA and other partners.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Its aim is to offer various programmes to support current information and communications technology (ICT) professionals and non-ICT professionals to upgrade and acquire new skills and domain knowledge.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It also allows employers in ICT and non-ICT companies who want to leverage TeSA programmes to attract fresh or mid-career professionals to their companies.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It can also help develop the number of ICM professionals which is prevalent in many sectors and can eventually empower traditional companies to improve performance.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Is it achieving its objectives and what are the next steps in the evolution of the programme?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: (In Mandarin):   Chairman, it has been four years since the National Translation Committee (NTC) was established in 2014.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: I would like the Minister to provide an update on the work of the Committee.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: In order to encourage Singaporeans to pay more attention to translation, Government agencies should take the lead.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Currently, the media and members of the public can check the standard translation of official terms from MCI's database.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: However, this glossary page was hidden in a remote corner of the MCI website, and people who are not aware of this service cannot find it at all.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: This database does not contain names of buildings and the streets either.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: A reader from Lianhe Zaobao recently pointed out that there were many translation errors with regard to the Chinese street names in the pamphlet distributed by a certain Town Council.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: There used to be standardised Chinese translation of street names, and the Singapore Land Authority (SLA) has published a Chinese version of the street directory before.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Currently, if the public wants to find the Chinese name of a certain street, they can go to the website of Street and Building Names Board (SBNB) under the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) to check.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: However, there were few people who are aware of such a service.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: To standardise the official translated names is the job of the Committee.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: However, after standardisation, if the public is still unaware of its existence, it would be such a waste.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: For the convenience of the media and the public, and to signal the Government's commitment in maintaining the standard of translation, I suggest an independent portal be set up, so that the public can check the official translated Government terms easily, including Chinese street names.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: If there are enough visits to the website, we will be able to collect enough data to develop this website into a machine translation system.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: As social media and messaging application platforms become more prevalent, the Ministry must tackle this problem head-on, and fast.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Last year, the Media Literacy Council organised the "Better Internet" campaign to promote responsible online habits and safe Internet use.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There is much we can learn from Australia, where the Office of the eSafety Commissioner is responsible for promoting online safety.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Office provides extensive resources on reporting of cyberbullying, helplines, online safety programmes and resources for schools and classrooms.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The first step we can take is to organise a centralised resource bank, as well as to create a safe space, for victims to take refuge in.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I urge the Ministry to consider this to tackle cyberbullying.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Their skills, knowledge and mindset determine if Singapore can succeed in the new digital economy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Our digital transformation is also only as meaningful as how it could make the lives of Singaporeans better.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This is also the heart of the digital transformation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The challenge is how we can help our workers to thrive in this new digital economy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: A worker in his mid-50s and has started working in 1980s has survived the typewriter, the pager, browsing using Netscape, emails on UNIX in the 1990s, rise of the mobile devices in the 2000s, the ongoing third industrial revolution on digital manufacturing, while trying to make sense of the Industrial Revolution 4.0, Internet of Things (IoT) and data exchange.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: How can MCI work with the tripartite partners to retrain and reskill workers and, in fact, also the employers, to take advantage of the opportunities brought forth by the digital economy?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: For there to be good jobs empowered by technology, there must be good companies similarly empowered.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: For SMEs, they need to develop a digital strategy and access competent manpower to execute the strategy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: However, SMEs might find it difficult to adequately resource this change.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The longer-term impact is impeded by digital growth and uneven development.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Can the Ministry develop a common pool of such technologies and manpower that these companies can tap on to accelerate participation in the digital economy?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: When I visited the Singapore Airport Terminal Services (SATS) Workers' Union members two weeks ago, I am convinced that technology will generally help our workers work longer and more productively.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Most of those I have met were in their 50s.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The backbreaking work of hauling luggage can never be fully eliminated because there are just too many different shapes of suitcases for automation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: But automated luggage drop-off can take away much of the physical work.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Part of the work now is to help passengers navigate and troubleshoot check-ins and drop-offs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The crux is early training and preparation, including for the subcontractors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Will the Ministry assist in ITMs to coordinate digital and technology preparation for workers and companies?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: How will MCI work with and incentivise employers to identify needed skills and train the workers ahead of digital transformation in the workplace?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Automation and the growth of the digital economy are inevitable.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This does not sound the death knell for the human worker.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Throughout history, mankind has weathered technological disruptions to find new jobs when there used to be none.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: But we have to be prepared to adapt and train even though history appears firmly on our side.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The consequence otherwise is a digital economy without a heart.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Chairman, the future is in digitalisation, as many of my colleagues have been pointing out.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The Government is taking the lead in going digital and, thanks to the efforts of the Government Technology Agency (GovTech), more and more Government functions are going online and getting tailored to our needs, making it easier and easier for us to use.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Everything, from tax returns to customs clearance, is amongst the easiest and most user-friendly in the world.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The Government is also providing extensive encouragement and support for SMEs to digitalise.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: It is likely that more and more will do so, both to provide better services for consumers and also to improve productivity for the shrinking workforce.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: However, the reality of digitalisation is that not everyone will be comfortable with the changes or able to adapt.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Many of us here may have already gone to the trouble of forgetting passwords and having 40 to 50 to remember.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: But these problems are minor, compared to those who may not have education, English in particular, and those who may not even be able to work on a computer.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: There are many, particularly the older and less educated, who have difficulty accessing some digital services.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Singapore has one of the highest mobile and Internet penetration rates.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: However, while the penetration is high, it is still not complete and there are many who are impecunious who do not have Internet access or mobile phones maybe because they have not paid their bills.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: So, this, too, may impede some of their access to mobile services.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: How can we ensure that Singaporeans of all ages and backgrounds are not left behind as the economy digitalises?

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Chairman, free-to-air TV channels in Singapore are now broadcast in both analogue and digital formats.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Of these, I suspect quite a lot of them are the elderly.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I would also like to know if it is possible for the Ministry to work with the Silver Generation ambassadors for them to educate the elderly about the need to have a digital TV set-top box and maybe assist elderly residents to set up the TV set-top box.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: This workgroup, comprising representatives from the public and private sectors, is to propose strategies to improve digital readiness among Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: It is important that we get our senior citizens to tap on technology to make their lives better.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: So, as we go on the Smart Nation drive, we must not forget to help our seniors to get ready for it, as Member Mr Yee Chia Hsing mentioned just now.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: In addition, may I also suggest that more be done for low-income families beyond what is being done now, in particular those with young children at home?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: What can we expect in terms of the recommendations?

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Chairman, firstly, let me declare my interests as I run the Asian business of a multinational media company, Fremantlemedia International.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: The mainstream media, to me, has perhaps the biggest and most important role to play in combating fake news in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: They also have a crucial role to play in strengthening social cohesion.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: These can be achieved through two pathways: enhancing the quality of journalism and building a network of partnerships.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: I am pleased that both Singapore Press Holdings (SPH) and Mediacorp are heading in these directions.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Editor-in-Chief of the SPH English/Malay and Tamil media group, Warren Fernandez, said recently that good journalism and news organisations that are credible and reliable play a vital role in combating fake news.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: This emphasis on quality journalism and credibility will ultimately also have important consequences for the company's bottom line as print circulation and advertising revenues continue to decline at SPH.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: One of the reasons for this turnaround was a focus on quality, in-depth journalism.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Mark Thompson said, and I quote, "We believe that more and more people are prepared to pay for high-quality in-depth journalism that helps them make sense of the world." An emphasis on balanced quality reporting and commentary will inevitably bring more subscribers and readers, be it for print or online.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: While reporting news quickly and accurately is important, Singaporeans would benefit from reading varied, considered commentaries that provide a deeper and sometimes alternative view of pressing national issues.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Mature, cogent and well-argued commentaries can deepen the level of debate and discussion among Singaporeans and also broaden the consciousness of the impact of certain arguments.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: It is about talent, and about nurturing and developing quality talent in the newsrooms.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: To me, the country needs more of quality commentators, such as The Straits Times Opinion Editor Chua Mui Hoong and Mediacorp journalist Barathi Jagdish.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: They raise questions like good journalists, but they do so constructively.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Their arguments are backed by facts and not just emotions.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Singaporeans today are bombarded by tidal waves of fake news and agenda-led emotional reactions of online bloggers and pseudo-journalists.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Many Singaporeans reading the personal ramblings of these so-called political-social commentators are not fully aware of the backstory and agendas of these sites and their contributors: online commentators who are more than happy to make inflammatory and controversial remarks to grow their readership for advertising revenues; commentators who insinuate without fear of any organisational sanction, and who are not bound by any code of ethics or journalistic ethos.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: When I was a rookie Malaysia Cup reporter in the early 1990s, the mentorship that I received from veteran football writer Jeffrey Low was invaluable.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: It played a key role in my development as a journalist and the stories I broke.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: That uncanny eye for detail, relationship building and the art of learning how to ask the right questions, these are things that cannot be learnt in the newsroom.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: They are learnt on the ground, on the job.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: There is a rich wealth of talent among veteran journalists in the newsrooms at SPH and Mediacorp, and we must encourage our newsrooms to tap on these senior journalists.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Old-school journalists can be terrifying to those who skate on the wrong side of law and ethics because they relied on investigative journalism and not Internet journalism.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: They did not have Google to help them look for information, nor did they report off stories posted on social media.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Instead, they spoke to people face-to-face, on the telephone, and developed their own network of contacts.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: They also checked their facts and corroborated news breaks.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: In a sea of emotional and sometimes irrational online commentaries, we must ensure that people are also provided with mature, well-argued opinions.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: We are beginning to see this renewed commitment to quality journalism by SPH and Mediacorp.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Programming on Channel NewsAsia consistently stands out because of a focus on quality.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Last year, we saw the documentary, "Regardless of Religion", the follow-up to the previous year’s hit, "Regardless of Race".

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Yet again, the producers treated a very difficult subject with sensitivity and made it entertaining and interesting.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: It helped that they had a natural talent to front the show.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary's ease in front of the camera was pivotal in the success of the programme.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: It is programmes like these that go a long way in setting the platform and developing social cohesion.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: And the recent changes at the Board and management level at Mediacorp have begun to show positive effects, with the company embarking on partnerships and looking to cement more.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Mediacorp will also have to look at partnering pay television platforms across the region and locally to elevate the quality and increase the footprint of its content.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Perhaps, the Government can look at incentive programmes for Mediacorp to achieve this.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: And I also agree that as important as these events are for the viewing public, we cannot be held to ransom to any ridiculous fee being asked for by rights holders.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: But as someone who has been on both sides of the fence – a rights holder and a buyer – I would like to suggest that the 2020 Olympics should be seen with a special lens.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: Other athletes, such as Quah Zheng Wen, will also be in their prime.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: It must have been difficult for Mediacorp to garner sponsorship and advertising, given the last-minute deal.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: If the deal had been brokered earlier, it would have given them more time to approach global sponsors of the Games, who are, as I speak, already planning their media spend for the Tokyo Olympics.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: If it is quality content, they will find a way to watch it.

speaker: Mr Ganesh Rajaram (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, the halo effect of Schooling’s win is still being felt two years after his feat.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Chairman, let me pick up on PSB programming.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: The PSB contestable funds scheme has been very important in developing quality local content across different languages – English, Malay, Tamil or Mandarin.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Shows that may not have been otherwise economically viable have been developed in Singapore and much appreciated by our own audience.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Many of these PSB programmes have been part of our television and have developed a very strong audience.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: While television remains a dominant medium, changing media consumption patterns have many viewers going online.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I must confess that I watch most of my own local programmes on Toggle.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Besides free-to-air TV, what other platforms is the Government working with to extend the reach of PSB programmes to engage Singaporeans?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Darryl David, you can take both your cuts together.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Media companies in Singapore include content creators in the film and/or television industries, 3D animation, cutting-edge video games, trans-media storytelling and new media initiatives.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Leading digital media companies, such as Lucasfilm, Tecmo-Koei, Double Negative, Electronic Arts and Ubisoft have also opened offices in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But what part can smaller media companies play in Singapore’s quest to be a global media hub?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If it is crucial to create a digitally-enabled media environment, what measures are there to help smaller media industry players take that digital journey of transformation?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Could the Government share how it is helping to build digital media capabilities needed for continued growth in the long term?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Mr Chairman, we would all agree that the library is and should always remain an important social and educational institution and that it has an important role to play in our new evolving economy.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How can we ensure that libraries remain viable and relevant in this new economy?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Can libraries better support the nationwide effort to promote and prepare all Singaporeans for the future economy so that jobseekers and entrepreneurs alike have access to ever-changing knowledge?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Beyond the computerisation of services and the development of technology to support reading, what can libraries do to make reading, whether it is traditional or digital, delightful and engaging for its users in all languages?

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
text: With a fast-ageing population, our libraries will face an uphill task to encourage reading among our seniors in the future.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
text: This challenge is further compounded by the fast pace of life and high-tech society in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
text: All these factors may have reduced the motivation for people to read in print, especially in the library.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
text: I wish to commend the efforts of the libraries in adopting many initiatives, such as mobile apps, reading clubs and e-books, to encourage reading.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
text: We must redesign our libraries to create more conducive learning corners for children and provide a more comfortable reading environment for adults, especially seniors.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
text: We must also make our libraries friendlier for the elderly and organise more regular activities, such as talks, to support active ageing.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
text: For example, Chiba Prefecture organises seminars on a regular basis for seniors on various topics that are relevant to the elderly.

speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
text: Hokkaido's libraries have partnered various senior welfare-related organisations, and provide many senior-friendly library services, such as book delivery services, "dementia café" and recitation services for those who are visually impaired.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Sun Xueling, you have half a minute.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Chairman, to tell the full story of a nation's history, it is not just the voices of important players which matter, but those of ordinary Singaporeans, too.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This will help preserve our heritage and also enrich the quality of our collections.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Further, how are we increasing access to archival resources in our libraries to encourage greater understanding of our history and culture?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Hon Members will be notified of the revised conclusion times for the subsequent Heads of Expenditure.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Head Q – Ministry of Communications and Information.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Mr Chairman, with your permission, I would like to show a short video summarising the work of my Ministry over the past year, and some slides throughout our responses.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: There are many examples of fellow Singaporeans embracing digital and harnessing opportunities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: One was in the video we just watched.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Ms Shakila Sham owns Eatz 19, a fusion restaurant.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: She decided to install a mobile ordering and payment solution, which allowed her customers to review the menu and order even before arriving at the restaurant, so they can avoid the queue.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This way, the customer is happy, and she was able to improve her operations with the data generated.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Most importantly, the added convenience made work more enjoyable for Shakila's wheelchair-bound employee, Suzy, who can now manage the ordering platform online, from home.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Another example is Mdm Santhiya Senthil Kumar, an avid self-learner.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: She attends coding classes with her son in the library.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This way, she can bond with her family and pick up a new skill in the process.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: She was able to apply her new skill to guide her son in coding his own games.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: There are many more Shakilas and Santhiyas out there.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Helping them do well is what drives all of us at the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI).

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In this Committee of Supply (COS), we will share with Members MCI's efforts to do so.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I will talk about our plans to develop our digital economy and enhance the digital readiness of Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary will elaborate on how workers, businesses and citizens can benefit from our digital economy and digital readiness efforts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat will explain MCI's efforts to transform and grow the media sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I will round up by sharing the wonderful transformation of our libraries, which should inspire us all.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Digital transformation is the most important issue facing businesses today.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Singapore Business Federation’s (SBF's) recent study showed that the majority of our businessmen fully appreciate the importance of digitalisation because the payoffs are enormous.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This is the context for our Smart Nation initiative – good jobs and opportunities for our people.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamad asked what the Government is doing to ensure that Singapore businesses and workforce can thrive in the digital future.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: My answer is "ABC" – Accelerate the digitalisation of existing sectors, Build up our infocomm media or infocomm media (ICM) companies, and Create future digital technology sectors.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But not all of the sectors have responded equally quickly.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Some sectors, like banking and finance, and retail, have done relatively well.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: During my recent visit to the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) FairPrice’s new "living lab" supermarket at SingPost Centre, I saw how FairPrice had transformed its traditional supermarket using innovative retail technologies to revolutionise the shopping experience to meet changing consumer expectations and habits in the digital age, while boosting workers’ productivity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But there are other sectors that are finding it more difficult to keep up.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Members asked how the Government can help small and medium enterprises (SMEs) benefit from digitalisation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Allow me to first share the common challenge that SMEs face in going digital.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: One reason why some sectors are unable to transform digitally is knowledge.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Even if companies are keen to embrace digitalisation, they do not know how to, or where to start.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This includes providing step-by-step guidance under the Industry Digital Plans (IDPs) to make digitalisation simpler for SMEs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We have since launched the Retail and Logistics IDPs last November and we aim to do more this year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Members asked about the outcomes of our initiatives to help SMEs digitalise.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Even though the programme has been operational for only less than a year, we are seeing encouraging results.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: A beneficiary of the pre-approved digital solution under the programme is House of Seafood, a restaurant chain and food manufacturer.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: However, each country has its own import requirements, and it was difficult to track them all efficiently.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, the company installed a digital tagging solution to automate the compliance checks for its many products.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The complexity of the logistics business cannot be underestimated.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, the company adopted an intelligent vehicle monitoring system to operate its vehicles better.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Fewer vehicle accidents mean better utilisation of assets.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This led to about 10% increase in the number of deliveries handled a day.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: To do so, we fully agree with Mr Teo Ser Luck that we must ensure that our programmes remain relevant in a fast-changing environment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will regularly review the IDPs and pre-approved solutions in the SMEs Go Digital Programme to ensure that they are in line with the latest industry trends and standards while meeting SMEs’ needs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamad asked what more can be done to help our SMEs seize the opportunities in digital.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Ms Sun Xueling asked if we would engage influential partners to help drive digitalisation within sectors.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: One initiative we are pursuing is to focus not just on individual solutions for individual SMEs, but to take a cluster approach by working with influential partners to help a group of SMEs from similar sectors.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will do more of such projects in the coming year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Ms Sun Xueling asked what sector-level initiatives do we have to drive digitalisation on a broader scale.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Last year, IMDA launched various innovative initiatives to support the digital transformation of both the logistics and retail sectors.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will help interested merchants in the core area of Kampong Glam, comprising about 200 merchants, adopt digital solutions to improve their business operations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This would include adopting integrated point-of-sale systems which enable cashless payments, inventory tracking and financial accounting.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: By automating these backend administrative processes, the merchants will have more time for their products and customers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We are working with StarHub on these business solutions for the merchants.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We are also enhancing the visitor experience by developing digital products, such as immersive walking trails, and working with Temasek Polytechnic School of Business to increase the merchants' online presence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We are partnering Grab to offer an additional cashless option and increase accessibility to the area.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: After all, the shops will benefit from more customers enjoying themselves in Kampong Glam.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Learning from the Kampong Glam project, we will explore how we could develop other projects to digitalise the retail sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Another way we are accelerating the sector's digitalisation is to put in place common infrastructure that will raise business productivity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Without an invoice, businesses do not get paid.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But invoicing can be very tedious and manual, with many inherent errors.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It can help businesses cut costs, ensure companies are paid faster and open up new financing options.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We are currently studying this with companies and will announce more details later.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This is necessary, because without a strong ICM sector to support businesses with good products, we will not go very far in our digitalisation journey.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In this respect, we want to have homegrown ICM companies, along with other companies supporting this sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamad asked about the plans to grow the ICM sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA has already launched the ICM Industry Transformation Map (ITM) last year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will do this by building up our workforce and helping our companies internationalise.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Most importantly, as digitalisation blurs traditional industry boundaries, we will help our companies reinvent themselves.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: One example is Y3 Technologies, a software solutions provider specialising in supply chain management solutions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In recent years, Y3 has transformed itself by moving away from just supply chain management to an innovative analytics service provider.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Thanks to its proprietary software, it now has 24/7 visibility of all customer orders, can handle a larger volume of orders and reduce the incidence of wrong delivery.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It has also used its analytics software products to diversify into complementary areas, such as e-commerce.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, we will do more to help our companies transform themselves like Y3.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Today, IMDA runs the Accreditation@SG Digital, which helps to scale innovative Singapore-based ICM companies to build deep capabilities locally and grow internationally.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will quadruple this in five years and avail more support to help them grow, including building their track record, assisting them to grow new growth capital and helping them to expand overseas.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In the case of Sense Infosys, an accredited local data analytics startup, IMDA's support in securing funding and facilitating key partnerships had contributed to the company’s overseas expansion and impressive growth.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: One way to build stronger ICM companies is to help them collaborate with end-users to build new and innovative solutions with potential to be scaled and exported.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA will focus their efforts in selected sectors first, including retail and logistics, to build up a community of solution providers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA will bring in expertise in technology areas, such as artificial intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT), to see how they can apply their technologies to business use cases.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I also announced a series of AI and data analytics initiatives.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As part of our ICM ITM, IMDA launched the AI Business Partnership Programme last November to bring companies interested in AI and AI solution providers together.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Although it is early days, IMDA has received promising problem statements from businesses across various sectors and is currently reviewing potential partnerships for co-funding.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA will share more details in the coming months.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA also launched the AI Apprenticeship Programme with AI Singapore to develop AI professionals through training courses.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Cedric Foo asked what Singapore is doing to prepare itself for the digital economy, including giving enterprises access to datasets for machine learning applications.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For instance, the Government has been actively improving data.gov.sg, its one-stop public portal for Government datasets, to include more useful datasets to enable businesses and citizens to co-create solutions using them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We are also reviewing the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) to keep pace with technological developments and regulatory trends to facilitate businesses’ use of personal data while safeguarding consumers' trust.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As more services and transactions take place online, it becomes even more important that they are digitally secure and reliable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Cybersecurity is thus a cornerstone of trust in our Smart Nation initiative.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Ms Sun Xueling asked if there are plans to assist businesses, including SMEs, and educate the public on how to prevent and respond to cybersecurity threats.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For instance, the Cyber Security Agency (CSA) is partnering the Association for Information Security Professionals (AISP) to equip our SMEs with cybersecurity knowledge so that they can better respond to cybersecurity threats like the ransomware attacks last year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: CSA also works with partners, such as the Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC), to raise awareness of the importance of cybersecurity and personal data protection among our students, and with IMDA and the National Library Board (NLB) to provide our seniors with infocomm training, which includes cybersecurity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Besides undergirding the digital economy, cybersecurity is also a growth engine.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This will create many exciting opportunities and jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Citi Singapore is one such company contributing to the cybersecurity ecosystem in our country.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Not many Members may know this, but the bank has established one of its two global security operations centre in Singapore, the other being in New York.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I visited the Singapore centre about two weeks ago.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: And there I met Mr Fadli Sidek, whom I had mentioned in my COS speech two years back.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Back then, he had overcome the disappointment of being rejected by a polytechnic and was working towards a cybersecurity degree.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Fadli is now a cyber threat intelligence analyst in Citi and he is doing well.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I was happy to see Fadli doing well and want to help more Singaporeans interested in cybersecurity to pursue their passions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: CSA will work with other partners to do so.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: First, CSA and IMDA are supporting the development of the Innovation Cybersecurity Ecosystem (ICE) at Block 71.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This initiative will be done with the National University of Singapore (NUS) and SingTel Innov8 and will help promising cybersecurity startups scale and internationalise.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This will catalyse the commercialisation and adoption of cybersecurity solutions to address emerging needs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In addition to cybersecurity, we will also invest to build up immersive media (IM) capability in Singapore, as we also see this as another promising area.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: First, we will advocate for IM adoption by facilitating business matching and information sharing to raise awareness on IM’s potential.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Second, to build innovation capacity by encouraging experimentation and development of proof of concepts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: And third, to develop talent for the IM industry.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat will share some of our efforts to build IM capabilities in his speech.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will announce more details of our plans for IM in the upcoming months.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For now, we have put together an IM exhibit for Members to experience how IM can transform the way we live and work in the digital future.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The first and most important is a strong workforce with the relevant expertise and skills.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Two years ago, I launched the TechSkills Accelerator (TeSA).

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Ruzaini was retrenched in 2015 after eight years in the industry.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As he was interested in cybersecurity, he tried to join the industry after his retrenchment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: However, he did not succeed as he lacked the formal training and qualifications.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Fortunately, he persisted and joined the Cybersecurity Associates and Technologists (CSAT) programme under the National Computer Systems (NCS), where he picked up new cybersecurity skills.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This will allow us to further develop our workforce for the digital economy.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Besides people, we also need to review our regulations in a fast-changing world to ensure they remain pro-business and fit for purpose.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Ong Teng Koon asked how IMDA will address the regulatory challenges in the converged ICM environment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: One salient issue in the converged ICM space is how digital technologies and social media platforms have come together to worsen the risk of fake news.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This was an area that MCI was studying in our review of the Broadcasting Act.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: However, as Parliament has just appointed the Select Committee on Deliberate Online Falsehoods to examine the issue, it would be better to study the Select Committee’s recommendations first before making further moves.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Dr Teo Ho Pin asked if there are plans to introduce regulations for AI applications.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Currently, we have no such plans as the field is still nascent and we want to avoid stifling innovation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But we do acknowledge public anxiety about AI.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IMDA is working with sector regulators to study issues and mitigate potential risks from deploying AI.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Besides talent and regulations, another enabler for a thriving digital economy is a conducive, rules-based international environment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: That is why we have advocated open data flows and facilitated cyber norms discussions in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As ASEAN Chairman this year, we will commit to improving digital literacy in ASEAN to help our people reap the benefits of digitalisation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Beyond ASEAN, we are also participating fully in international mechanisms to provide digital flows.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: When our certification scheme is in place, certified organisations in Singapore will be able to exchange personal data with certified organisations in participating APEC economies much more seamlessly, while consumers can be assured that the cross-border transfer of their personal data will be subject to high standards of data protection.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: And that is the main focus of our digital readiness efforts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Ultimately, Smart Nation is not just a series of technology projects.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is a whole-of-nation movement to improve the lives of all Singaporeans in the digital age.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As Minister Vivian Balakrishnan had said earlier, our approach will, therefore, be inclusive by design.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary will elaborate later on this.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is up to us to seize them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Everyone will have a role to play in our broader digital transformation, and we, at MCI, will work with everyone to ensure that we all gain from this shared journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Chairman, the emergence of new opportunities in the digital age is why Singapore is transforming itself into a Smart Nation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Smart Nation is about making all our lives easier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is about building a strong society and economy with opportunities for all, and where businesses thrive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is important that no one gets left behind as the world becomes increasingly digital.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked about how the Government will work with businesses and the community to help citizens with this transition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is not the first time that Singapore is experiencing a technology-driven transformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Since the 1980s, we have introduced information technology (IT) in schools, made broadband available to all homes, and transformed many public services using technology and the Internet.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As the pace of technological change accelerates, we will need a more comprehensive and inclusive approach to ensure that all Singaporeans can participate in and benefit from the opportunities of a digital age.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To do so, we need to help citizens be digitally ready.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There are three important principles that guide our approach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The user interface of our digital services and applications must be so easy to use that almost everybody can start using it with little or no instruction.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, we have many programmes that focus on giving people access to affordable devices and the Internet.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But being digitally ready is also about having the skills to use digital technology safely and confidently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These include basic information and media literacy skills, awareness of cybersecurity and personal data protection, and several other skills as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Being digitally ready means ensuring that Singaporeans have, firstly, digital access, which is the means to transact digitally; secondly, digital literacy, which is the skills, attitudes and values of a digital citizen; all of which will, ultimately, lead to digital participation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As an example of the sort of issues we are concerned about for digital access is smartphones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: A smartphone becomes a key enabler for many of the digital services that we want to provide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: How can we ensure that enough Singaporeans have adequate access?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Once we ensure there is adequate access, we need to develop a base of digital literacy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To begin with, we will articulate a set of basic digital skills, that is, skills that every one of us should have as a first step towards being able to participate in a digital society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The focus areas of these skills will be the ability to communicate, transact and search for information through a mobile device for day-to-day living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These skills will be articulated as a curriculum that will be made available to training providers and can also be used by family and friends or community partners who are interested in helping everyone enjoy the benefits of our Smart Nation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh asked about the Government’s efforts in tackling cyberbullying.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We agree with Assoc Prof Goh that it is important that we have avenues where the youths, their parents and their teachers can seek help and support from credible sources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Help123 was initiated last year by the National Council of Social Service and various partners like Fei Yue Community Services and TOUCH Community Services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It provides services for youth cyber-wellness issues a dedicated webchat, email service and a hotline.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It also provides resources of counsellors who are able to support people who need further direct intervention and help.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Media Literacy Council also does work in this space.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It makes available and will continue to produce resources to tackle cyberbullying.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Examples include an anti-cyberbullying instructional video as part of the "Better Internet" campaign, informational packages with information specific for victims to counter cyberbullying, products, such as those providing guidance for parents and families to detect the symptoms of cyberbullying, and also to provide help to children.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: A series of workshops is being rolled out this year to help parents raise digitally resilient children.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Vikram Nair asked how we can ensure that Singaporeans of all ages do not get left behind.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our approach has always been to be as inclusive as possible but recognising that some groups would find the transition difficult and providing them with targeted help.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will continue to help the elderly by expanding digital readiness initiatives for seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Yee Chia Hsing asked whether more can be done to prepare elderly residents for digital television (TV).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Just as we will help citizens become digitally ready, the Government will also help workers and businesses build strong capabilities to benefit from the opportunities in a digital economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked about the progress of TeSA and its upcoming evolution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: TeSA is a key tripartite initiative to help build strong digital capabilities through training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will provide more training places, more programmes and will address more user sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: TeSA is a key initiative not just for the workers, but also for the businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One of the key issues about the development of the digital economy is going to be the provision of capabilities and skills in the workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, by our focus on TeSA, we are helping workers find jobs and transition into new jobs, and we are helping businesses develop the skills and capabilities to help them grow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will require and build upon the strong multi-agency and tripartite approach that we have taken.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There will be more job opportunities that demand such frontier technology skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Up to now, a significant part of what TeSA has been doing is concentrating on the existing skills gaps, existing jobs gaps, known technologies, well-developed and mature business issues, and we need to push towards these frontier technologies to try and anticipate what would be the next steps required to grow our digital economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I hope many more companies will work with TeSA to co-develop training programmes in these areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Thirdly, we will widen our approach towards more user sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Information and communication technology (ICT) professionals are in demand across many economic sectors, as the economy and industries rapidly digitalise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Currently, TeSA is quite focused on the ICT sector, as well as on the Finance and Healthcare sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Moving forward, TeSA will expand its training offering into Manufacturing and Professional Services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In line with our commitment to develop our people, TeSA will also strengthen our support for those who might need it most, such as mid-career ICT PMETs in search of new job opportunities as the economy and the ICT job landscape evolve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Desmond Choo asked about how we can better support workers, especially mature ones, to reskill and upskill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Since 2016, approximately 10,000 TeSA training places have been taken up by those above the age of 40.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But TeSA will do more to support more mid-career ICT PMETs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: First, we will help to curate cross-sector ICT job openings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: While there are ICT job openings in the public, non-profit and private sectors, as well as across different industry sectors, many mid-career ICT PMETs are unlikely to possess the networks, contacts or the sector-specific skills needed to make the transition into new sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They may already have skills which are relevant to either the private, public or the non-profit sector, or they may have ICT skills that are domain-specific to a given industry within the economy.
