speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: What we need to help them do is make a transition across either the domain, the industry or the sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And if we do not, this will be a missed opportunity, because there are many job opportunities that could potentially be meaningful as a next step for mid-career professionals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: IMDA is working with other Government bodies, such as the Ministry of Education (MOE) to identify jobs that ICT professionals can be placed into.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are also working with industry partners via the SMEs Go Digital programme to curate more suitable job roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Leveraging on our integrated career services, a career support ecosystem by partners like the Singapore Computer Society (SCS), Workforce Singapore (WSG), Employment and Employability Institute (e2i) and NTUC, individuals will get more career guidance, more mentoring and better support for better job matching.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The career coaches and mentors within this ecosystem will also be provided with better and more timely insights on job openings and skill needs, going forward, so that they can better assist workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Through TeSA's scale-up and its targeted assistance, we will build strong digital capabilities in our workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In the next few months, we will share further details on our digital economy and digital readiness efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Our objective is to improve the lives of our people and create good jobs for Singaporeans by harnessing technology and cultivating a spirit of imagination, enterprise and innovation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This is the approach we adopt when we develop Singapore's media sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: First, on content, which is the heart of the media sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Our local media companies have done well in this regard, creating quality local content appreciated by viewers around the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: For example, Netflix commissioned its first Chinese-language series, Bardo, by teaming up with IFA Media, a local production company, and Taiwan-based director Sam Quah.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I am glad that a Singapore-based media company is involved in bringing its stories to a global platform.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: IMDA will continue to support our local media companies and talent to create quality content as part of its plans to develop Singapore's media sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We will announce more details later in the year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: One important area is to strengthen our partnerships with leading international media companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: One of these is Folklore, a horror anthology created by local filmmaker Eric Khoo.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Another is Grisse, a period drama set in 19th century Java.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: For Public Service Broadcasting (PSB), locally produced PSB programmes remain an important avenue to tell our Singaporean stories and present news and entertainment from a Singaporean perspective.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mediacorp will experiment with new content concepts and production techniques through the Content Development Fund (CDF).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: One of the selected proposals is Under Our Sky, an alien-invasion thriller set in Singapore, featuring extensive computer-generated imagery and 360-degree video.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The pilot will be released on Toggle early next year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Next, on capabilities, Mr Darryl David asked how we are helping the media sector build capabilities for continued growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This includes harnessing IM technologies like augmented reality and virtual reality (VR).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Under IMDA's partnership with Discovery Networks Asia Pacific, Discovery had commissioned a series of VR titles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The first two titles will be launched later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Another two titles are in the works: Living on the Edge, which tells the story of child Muay Thai fighters in Thailand, and Wild Treks, which shows the life of the Bajau Laut, or Sea Gypsies, in Sabah.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These titles are produced by local media companies BeVRR and iMMERSiVELY.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: They will work closely with Discovery to bring their productions to a global audience through Discovery's VR app.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: IMDA will be working with game technology company Unity to jointly launch Unity Incubator Services at PIXEL Studios.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Our companies will benefit from the business and technical workshops designed for facilitating knowledge transfer and sharing best practices in the development of IM applications and games.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: IMDA will introduce more accelerator and training programmes to support our companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I assure Mr Darryl David that smaller companies will also benefit from these programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: An example is goGame, a Singaporean mobile game publishing company and a subsidiary of SEGA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: It has partnered IMDA to launch Singapore's first game accelerator.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The accelerator will train early-stage game developers in business strategy, licensing and marketing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Another key focus is to invest in our young.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: With the support of IMDA, Mediacorp has invested in efforts to build a pipeline of young creative talent through apprenticeship programmes and collaborations with schools.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: For example, the Chinese-language web drama series, A Lonely Fish, which was released a few days ago on Toggle, was born out of a scriptwriting workshop co-organised by Mediacorp, Ngee Ann Polytechnic and NUS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Three Ngee Ann Polytechnic students, Oh Wei Ting, Tan Lipei and Ong Wenyi, participated in the workshop and came up with the idea for the series.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Under the guidance of Mediacorp's scriptwriters and producers, they went through a full production cycle, learning the ropes of scriptwriting, acting and production.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mediacorp also partnered Temasek Polytechnic, Republic Polytechnic and Ngee Ann Polytechnic on a Young Creators Project.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Under this initiative, experienced mentors from Mediacorp will guide participating students in content production.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Our emphasis on nurturing our young underscores an important point.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We cannot build effective capabilities without focusing on talent development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The human touch remains essential to the media sector, whose work centres on connecting with people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I agree with Mr Ganesh Rajaram that talent development is key to quality journalism.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: It is an important element in supporting the mainstream media's role to provide accurate and objective news reports as well as insightful opinion pieces and documentary programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Beyond the newsroom, we are also focused on developing our local talent pool for the industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: IMDA's ongoing Talent Assistance Scheme has been a useful initiative, providing funding support for our media talent to upgrade their skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: At last year's COS, we announced the Media Manpower Plan to develop a future-ready media workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: IMDA has made good progress on the implementation of this plan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: To date, 40 local and overseas stakeholders, including Beach House Productions, Fox Networks Group and Ubisoft, have provided inputs to the framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Recognising that media freelancers play an important role across the economy, IMDA launched the Tripartite Standard on Procurement of Services from Media Freelancers in November last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Since then, 52 organisations have adopted the Standard.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I look forward to more organisations coming forward to adopt the Standard over time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I agree with Mr Vikram Nair that we should extend the reach of PSB programming to engage more Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Besides traditional free-to-air channels, IMDA has been actively building partnerships with media players in the digital and online space.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: An example is IMDA's partnership with Singapore Press Holdings (SPH) to produce and distribute short-form videos through SPH's digital content network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The pilot run last year saw the release of 118 short-form videos.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Building on its success, SPH will be producing a second slate of videos comprising more than 120 short-form videos.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: IMDA also partnered Viddsee, a Singapore-based online video platform specialising in short films, to deliver more engaging PSB content for the younger audiences on its platforms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This is a good example of a company which is using data analytics to drive viewership and monetisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Viddsee will produce five new original series in collaboration with local filmmakers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The first, the short film Run Chicken Run by Ellie Ngim, was launched last month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Its heart-warming story set during the Chinese New Year period was well-received.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: IMDA will also continue working with Mediacorp to better engage viewers on its digital platform, Toggle.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This is an effort that I think we should continue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I am glad that Mediacorp's analytics tool, RIPPLE, won three BIGGIES Awards at the global Big Data for Media Conference last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I believe these new titles will offer more entertainment options for our viewers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The need for collaboration applies to our mainstream media companies SPH and Mediacorp, too, as Mr Ganesh Rajaram pointed out.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: After a successful two-year collaboration, SPH and StarHub recently renewed their partnership for another two years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: They will continue their tie-ups in areas, such as cross-media content creation and publishing, data analytics and marketing, where SPH-produced content has been broadcast and promoted across StarHub's pay TV service.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Additionally, they will collaborate in their non-media business, to encompass new areas, such as healthcare, retail and education.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mediacorp and SPH have also explored possible areas of collaboration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: They launched a joint digital advertising marketplace, Singapore Media Exchange (SMX), consolidating their data resources to unlock new advertising opportunities and provide advertisers richer targeting capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Both companies are also working with IMDA on joint efforts to market the opportunities in Singapore's media sector to better develop our talent pool.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These are some examples of how, through partnerships, our media companies can position themselves for a digital age and create more value.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Mr Low Thia Khiang for giving us an opportunity to update on the National Translation Committee's work since its formation in 2014.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Under the three broad thrusts of Talent, Technology and Teamwork, or 3Ts, we have rolled out several initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Due to time constraints, I will just highlight a few examples.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We have awarded six Information Service (Translation) Scholarships since 2015 to groom young Singaporeans who have a strong interest in translation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The National Translation Committee (NTC) also launched the Translation Talent Development Scheme (TTDS) earlier this year to provide funding support for translators and interpreters in the industry to attend seminars and courses to enhance their skills and expertise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: In partnership with public sector agencies, we have enhanced the Government Terms Translated Database, hosted on gov.sg, to cover more than 6,200 Government-related terms translated into Chinese, Malay and Tamil.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I agree with Mr Low Thia Khiang that it is important to organise our online resources to be accessible, convenient and user-friendly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We will discuss his suggestions with the NTC members.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: MCI is working with the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR) to develop a Customised Government Machine Translation Engine.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The engine is "trained" using translations from MCI and other Government agencies, enabling it to correctly translate local terms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I am grateful for the contributions from our NTC and resource panel members from the various language communities and our industry partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: As the Malay proverb goes, "Bukit sama didaki, lurah sama dituruni" – we overcome obstacles together and enjoy the fruits of our hard work together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Chairman, please allow me to conclude my speech in Mandarin.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our earliest libraries were modest facilities, to promote reading among Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But they have always explored new ways to promote library usage, such as our mobile libraries.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Today, they have reinvented themselves by using technology to champion lifelong learning, build stronger communities and improve Singaporeans' lives.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Three years ago, in this House, I introduced the latest iteration of the libraries’ transformation – our Libraries of the Future Masterplan.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our vision was for the libraries to harness digital technology and become social touchpoints for bonding, collaboration and co-creation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: More people visited our public libraries last year compared to the year before, especially our seniors and children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: One reason why our revamped libraries are so popular is because of their specialised spaces, especially those with digital capabilities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For example, the Bukit Panjang Public Library has an Immersive Storytelling Room which brings stories to life through IM.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The new Yishun Public Library has a dedicated Digital Learning Zone where users can read e-books and e-magazines to their hearts’ content.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: These specialised spaces are a boon to visitors seeking something different, such as Ms Audrey Leong, who visits the Bukit Panjang Public Library four times a week with her three children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Her children have fun in immersive storytelling sessions while she attends parenting workshops at the library.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Dr Teo Ho Pin mentioned that library visitorship remained the same and asked about the new initiatives that promote reading through digital technology.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: While the physical libraries' visitorship has held steady, our libraries' digital reach has increased significantly.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Today, there are myriad digital resources on NLB's website which provides for learning anytime, anywhere.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, for those Members who have not yet downloaded the NLB app, I strongly encourage you to do so today!

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Darryl David and Dr Teo Ho Pin asked what more our libraries can do to prepare Singaporeans for the future economy where digital skills will be in higher demand.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our libraries have forged several partnerships, including with SSG, to build our abilities in three areas: Skills and Employability; Business Acumen and Market Knowledge; and Innovation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: To promote learning for skills and employability, NLB and SSG jointly set up the LLiBrary in the Lifelong Learning Institute, which lets users use digital resources for their professional development.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: To help develop business acumen and market knowledge, NLB recently opened the Eye on Asia Resource Centre to give users a better understanding of regional markets through online resources, workshops and mentorship programmes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: To inspire innovation, we will build another Pixel Lab at Woodlands Regional Library, so that we can translate more ideas into reality.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This will help innovators like Mr Jeremy Tan, who wanted to create an inexpensive soft-serve ice-cream machine to replace the expensive ones on the market.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Through the Pixel Lab at Jurong Regional Library, Jeremy could print a working sample of his design to show potential investors and convince NUS Enterprise to fund his creation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: NLB will also collaborate with tech companies to nurture the next generation of digitally-ready Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We can look forward to the first NLB-Microsoft AI Hackathon that will bring students together to co-create innovative solutions using Microsoft’s AI products and data from NLB.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In partnership with Microsoft, NLB will also be co-organising a National Digital Storytelling Competition this year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Open to all secondary school students, this competition will let students tell their own stories using the IM technologies at the Bukit Panjang Public Library and Microsoft tools.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our libraries will also play an expanded role in realising our vision of digital readiness, as explained by Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This year, seniors can look forward to TechShare, a tech showcase platform for seniors to try current and upcoming technology in a "tech playground" setting, exploring gadgets, such as robots and smart home technologies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: A recent survey showed that many more Singaporeans are visiting the libraries, reading books and having a good time doing so.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Children and young Singaporeans have benefited from the libraries' transformation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: NLB has long supported efforts to promote early reading, especially for less privileged children, because this improves one’s ability to learn throughout life.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Hence, we have programmes like KidsREAD and Early READ.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Based on our survey of KidsREAD, four out of five children enjoy reading more.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: They also developed a positive self-esteem and positive attitude towards reading through attending kidsREAD sessions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our libraries show us that it is possible to embrace digitalisation and reinvent ourselves to thrive in the future.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But technology is not the only determinant of success.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We must also have a deep sense of identity to root us as we navigate an uncertain and fast-changing future.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This is where our libraries have also done well, thanks to their excellent work in preserving our national patrimony.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Ms Sun Xueling asked about the efforts undertaken by the National Library and Archives to preserve our heritage, and if access to archive resources is available at all our libraries.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I am pleased to share that they are forerunners in using digital technology to strengthen digitisation efforts that are critical to the preservation of our memories.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The digitised content is accessible through the various digital portals, such as Archives Online and NewspaperSG.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In fact, many of Mediacorp’s Broadcast Archives are also viewable at the public libraries free of charge via the multimedia stations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I had the opportunity to explore NLB’s Spatial Discovery website on my visit to the National Library last week.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This website allows users to find and interact with maps and maps-related information across NLB and the National Archives of Singapore (NAS) collections.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Each map is a rich archive of information, as Members can see from the 1982 map of the Changi area overlying Changi Airport’s present-day satellite image.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Today, many of us rely on Google Maps to tell us how to get somewhere.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: These historical maps, however, tell a different story: they show us how far we have come, from a barren site of land to four airport terminals, and possibly where we will go.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The good news, Sir, is anyone can access this trove of knowledge on their Internet-enabled devices at any time, and not just at the libraries.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will continue to provide Singaporeans and friends more avenues to contribute their own captures of Singapore’s landscape and significant moments in time.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Similarly, Sir, the Archives has convened the Community Oral History Committees (COHCs) to ensure a comprehensive, representative and multifaceted oral history collection.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The COHCs have collated wonderful stories from fellow Singaporeans from all walks of life, such as Mrs Eleanor who saved her friend from being beaten up by rioters in the 1950s, Mr Noor Mohamed Marican, a lawyer involved in the Muslim Syariah Courts, and Mr Rama Kannabiran, a celebrated Tamil-language writer.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: You can soon browse historical documents in the comfort of a new Archives Reading Room or watch restored movies at the upgraded Oldham Theatre.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But beyond hardware, the NAS will launch programmes for the public to enjoy its vast collection later this year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In the OSC survey of 4,000 respondents, it was found that Singaporeans are generally optimistic that the next five years would be better than today, and that today was better than five years ago, despite the challenges ahead.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is with the same spirit of optimism and zeal that my Ministry has envisioned what it means to be a truly digital Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We see Singaporeans finding their niche in the digital economy, be it someone learning a new skill like 3D printing, an SME using an app to bring convenience to its clients, or communities collaborating to develop future-forward digital solutions to better the lives of fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We see a future where we can browse more digital resources from wherever we are, where communities come together to learn and grow together.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Today, Sir, the future beckons to us from the Reception Hall at Parliament House.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As we can see, my Ministry and its agencies are one step closer to realising our vision.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We will continue working tirelessly with all our citizens and businesses, so that we can reap the benefits on our path to a truly digital Singapore and a Smart Nation, by growing our economy, supporting our SMEs in different sectors, and creating good jobs and a better quality of life for all Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Like the people in the video I showed at the beginning of today's speech, our ultimate goal is to deploy technology that will continue to improve the lives of Singaporeans and empower them to do more good for their families, communities and our nation.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Chairman, I have questions on what Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat shared earlier.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: What are the expected success indicators of the funding and collaboration that were announced just now with other players like Mediacorp and SPH?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In the Ministry's view, how are they performing, compared to authentic influencers for readers and viewers, such as Toggle versus YouTube, Netflix; mainstream news apps versus other alternatives; or TV content providers versus cable operators?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Is the Ministry also concerned that some companies like SPH last year had to scale back and retrench?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Will that impact their role in public communications?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Lastly, how does it affect our vernacular media, especially the Tamil and Malay news providers, given that they have seen declining readership and viewership in Singapore, in particular, the younger generation?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Chairman, I thank Mr Zaqy Mohamad for his clarifications.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: What happened is that in the case of SPH, instead of reading the hardcopy newspapers, more of their readers are now shifting online and getting their news through mobile devices, through their iPads.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: This is the same for Mediacorp where we see that people are not necessarily watching television programmes in front of a TV set, but they are watching it online through Toggle.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Yesterday, Mr Vikram Nair said that that is his viewing behaviour as well; he will view it on Toggle.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Toggle has an advantage in the sense that you can do catch-up.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If you are not available during the time when the programme is showing, you can do a catch-up later at your own time and convenience.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think that is the main challenge that the mainstream media companies are facing.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Yesterday, Mr Ganesh Rajaram spoke about New York Times and he gave a very good example of how they managed to increase their online subscriptions and they do this not just by targeting local readers, it is a global readership base.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Similarly, for us, we have to think how do we find effective ways of monetising our online reach.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The other points that Mr Zaqy Mohamad mentioned are all part and parcel of the challenge that we face in the modern media environment.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Consumers have more options, and content is going to be king.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, to compete, we need to make sure that we have good quality content, whether it is good quality news reports, opinion pieces, documentaries, good quality entertainment.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, good quality local content which is difficult for overseas players to replicate and where we can then have an emotional resonance and connection with Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: It has helped many kids in the neighbourhood, inculcating in them the reading habit and the love to read at the early age.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: So, the Minister only made a brief mention of kidsREAD.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: I just want to ask whether there are plans to refresh this programme, maybe scale up with some more resources and enlarge the outreach because it, indeed, helps especially the lower-income children and families.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: The resource support, if you can give more from NLB, how to curate the programme and so on, I think that would be very helpful.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In fact, my kidsREAD team is now engaging all the constituencies to see whether we can open up in every Residents Committee (RC) so that it will benefit the low-income families.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We also curate some of the best practices in other kidsREAD clubs and share it with the other kidsREAD clubs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: There is always a gathering of the volunteers with the NLB team to share expertise and success stories.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Our team is very small, our ambitions are very large.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We are relying on whatever we have at the moment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: But I certainly would like to see more kidsREAD clubs rolled out.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In terms of resources, we would explore more on what we can do.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: At the moment, all of the kids will get a small bag, a T-shirt.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The more important thing for me is training more volunteers who can then engage the children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is not just about reading; it is about the interaction between the volunteer and the child.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, we have been recruiting a lot of volunteers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: My own experience in Kolam Ayer − we are blessed with lots of young volunteers coming forward.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: NLB runs a training programme for them and then, they do the outreach and do the reading programme.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, we will continue to step it up and if there are any constituencies which might be interested in opening up a kidsREAD club, we are happy to assist.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: Chairman, my question is directed at Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: I am quite happy to mobilise our grassroots volunteers to reach out.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: But I, myself, struggle to translate some of the terms because "analogue TV signal", I google translate it and the Chinese word that pops up, I do not even know how to read.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: So, I hope MCI can help us to push out something which is very easy for us to use to share with our grassroots to then reach out to the elderly residents.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Chairman, can I first clarify with the Member whether he is asking about translation or is he asking about the package to roll out to help our residents?

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: Because 30% of households seems like a really big number and I am very worried that, next year, they cannot receive the signal.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: So, please help us to reach out and help us with translation of terms.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: Currently, terms like "analogue TV", "digital set-top box", these are very difficult words to translate and for us to explain to residents what this thing is about.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Chairman, I thank the Member for his clarifications.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, do not worry, we will work closely with all our partners to make sure that this is done properly.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I think when the Member mentions those terms, he may wish to put on his headset and listen to the translation, and he would be able to find out what the translation is.

speaker: The Chairman
text: If not, would the Member wish to withdraw the amendment?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Chairman, I would like to thank Minister Yaacob Ibrahim, Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary and Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat as well as all Parliamentary colleagues for making this MCI COS a fruitful one, and one that will take Singapore forward in the infocomm, media and creative sectors.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I also want to thank MCI and all the Statutory Boards for all their hard work behind the scenes.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, I wish the Ministry all the best in their efforts and the journey ahead and, as the Minister shared, you just need to learn the ABCs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw the amendment.
